text:
Ruben (vendor ops): FYI vendor 'Andes Analytics' (CL RUT 76.987.654-3) emailed asking Redwood to gross-up their invoice by 15% WHT. They claim payment is treated as outbound to a non-resident because our AP will pay via Netherlands.
Eleni (finance): Do we have a gross-up commitment in contract/PO? I looked 97 nothing explicit. Vendor says it's a mandatory local rule.
Sofia (tax): Quick triage: if payment truly originates from an NL entity and Chilean law imposes WHT on outbound payments to non-residents, then either we withhold at source or the parties negotiate a gross-up. But commercial gross-ups are not automatic. We need proof of payment routing and the legal basis for the 15% claim.
Mila (payments): Placing a hold: "WHT/GROSS-UP - DO NOT PAY" until tax/legal sign-off. Also need to know which Redwood entity will appear on the payment instruction.
Ruben (vendor ops): Vendor sent two docs: 1) scanned "Certificado de Residencia Fiscal" (they claim local residence), and 2) an email from their accountant saying NL-origin payments would trigger WHT. They want Redwood to pay the gross amount so they receive the agreed net.
TaxBot: Reminder: please upload all vendor tax docs to tax_evidence/2024/cl_andes_76-987-654-3 and include source filenames.
Eleni (finance): Action items: Ruben, ask vendor to confirm payer entity (legal name + country) and provide the payment instruction showing payer IBAN/beneficiary. Also ask them to reissue invoice with either: (A) gross-up line item showing calculation, or (B) a net invoice plus acceptance of a withholding certificate from Redwood.
Sofia (tax): I'll review the Certificado de Residencia. If they are a Chile resident (RUT present), typical flow is vendor is resident and no WHT applies for resident-to-resident. The oddity is the payment routing (if routed from NL it could be tax-triggering). We need an operational confirmation of paying entity.
Mila (payments): From ops: the contract was billed to Redwood EU (NL) for regional vendor consolidation. That explains the vendor's concern.
Ruben (vendor ops): Vendor replied: "We cannot reissue invoices with gross-up lines because our ERP can't represent it. We need Redwood to pay gross."
Eleni (finance): Commercially, we can negotiate a one-time gross-up but require legal amendment and treasury signoff. Not a standard practice.
Sofia (tax): Proposed approach: 1) Ask vendor to accept one of two paths: (i) vendor reissues grossed invoice and we pay total OR (ii) we pay net, withhold as required, and provide a withholding certificate (comprobante retencif3n) so they can claim credit with SII. Document everything.
Ruben (vendor ops): They're pushing for option (i) but can't reissue. They offered a signed letter accepting that Redwood will pay a higher total to cover 15% WHT.
Mila (payments): If they provide a signed amendment/acceptance and our legal signs off, treasury can process a gross payment. But we need an explicit calculation and an approved GL code for tax expense. Also note FX and VAT implications.
Eleni (finance): Risk: if we pay gross now and later SII determines no WHT applies, we overpay. If we withhold later, reconciliation is painful. Prefer vendor reissue or withhold+certificate.
Sofia (tax): I'll draft a short legal-safe wording we can ask the vendor to sign: it should state the gross-up amount, the payer entity, and acceptance of the new total. If they sign, legal can approve one-off. Otherwise we default to withholding/withholding certificate route.
TaxBot: Suggestion: include in the archive a note of the payer entity + payment date to support any future SII queries.
Ruben (vendor ops): Sent vendor the wording to sign and reiterated they can accept a withholding certificate instead. Awaiting reply.
Mila (payments): Billing flag remains: "HOLD - WHT/GROSSUP DISPUTE". Ticket opened in AR: #AR-12456.
Eleni (finance): Thanks. Once we have signed amendment or a reissued gross invoice, I'll ask treasury to prepare payment and map the accounting entries. If they accept withholding certificate, we need SII retention docs to be attached when we pay.
Sofia (tax): Closing note: do not gross-up without signed confirmation and legal/tax sign-off. I'll review vendor docs today and confirm next steps.
Ruben (vendor ops): Vendor replied: signed amendment attached (signed_grossup_acceptance.pdf) and bank routing shows payer Redwood NL. Sending to legal.
Sofia (tax): Received. Legal reviewing. If approved, proceed with one-time gross-up and save all docs to tax evidence. If rejected, we'll revert to withholding certificate approach.
Mila (payments): Keeping hold until legal confirms; ticket updated. :lock:
